meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'd like to know why my son got a zero on his Hamlet essay before anyone called me.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
"This record is what we have." Your own procedure says you speak to Owen first, so the zero comes off while he answers it. And whatever happens, this stays off his record and stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Give me the play, I'll search it myself. Students misquote Shakespeare all the time. A wrong line is a wrong line, and it doesn't tell you who typed it.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I don't find it in the scene. What else do you have, and what are you proposing for the zero?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. And you still haven't told me what you're proposing for the zero.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private, before December 1, with nothing on his record. I want that in writing tonight, and what I think of your outline goes in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put the time and the room in the same email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 after school, before December 1, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want the time and room confirmed in writing, and my concerns about the outline comparison answered. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the terms in writing tonight with the time and room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You told her to search the scene in the play herself and she found the quoted line wasn't there, because that was something she could check on the spot rather than take on your word.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero unanswered, so she stayed on procedure and kept pressing for the zero to come off.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the blank document at 11:31 PM and the text arriving minutes later on the night before it was due, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay by itself, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument between an outline and an essay, answer that right then, for instance by saying what the change shows and offering to look at any draft with a date, before moving on to the rewrite.
